turns.text: I'd like to practise a hard parent meeting. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. I'll send END MEETING on its own when I want to stop. I'm Owen's English teacher, and Meredith has just walked into my classroom.
Why am I here instead of at my desk? Owen's essay.
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
What you found. Before or after anyone called me?
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.
Created. Not written, created. What else is in that history?
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
Pasted from where? Kids move drafts between documents all the time. I'll want that history on paper, and you still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
I'm not here for your respect. The history, on paper. Today.
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.
A misquote is a student getting a line wrong from memory. Show me where it sits in his essay, and name the three editions so I can check them myself.
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
I'm not here to be complimented. The three editions, and the page in his essay. Now.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.
Students change their minds when they research. That's called revising. Put the outline in front of me, with Owen's name and the date on it.
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.
That's a machine's guess, and the company that makes it says never to act on it alone. Your own procedure says the same. Now the outline and the editions, on paper.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
Is Hale asking me how to do Hale's job? There's no off the record. I'd withdraw the zero today and put it in writing.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.
That's 4.4, and it would be in writing. But so far you've told me things and shown me nothing, and the zero is still in the gradebook. Put the history, the outline and the editions in front of me.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? You're asking me that, with Owen's zero still sitting in the gradebook. The history, the outline, the editions.
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.
"The zero stands." Go ahead, Hale, I'm going to the principal's office myself, and I'll have that sentence in writing first. Show me one page I can check, or we're done.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Neither. The zero comes off, and you show me a page I can check.
